title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: f: X -> S is smooth and proper of relative dimension 1 (a family of curves of genus g) in characteristic p. The page continues the previous one, which built a canonical description of the Cartier isomorphism via p-bases and ended by asking for a 'global cohomological definition' for curves.

Grothendieck writes the two filtrations of H^1_DR = R^1f_*(Omega^._{X/S}) as one cross-shaped diagram.

(1) The vertical column is the Hodge filtration: 0 -> f_*Omega^1_{X/S} -> H^1_DR -> R^1f_*O_X -> 0. It is exact because Hodge-de Rham degenerates for curves.

(2) The horizontal row is the conjugate filtration: 0 -> R^1f_*(O_X)^{(p)} --alpha--> H^1_DR --beta--> f_*(Omega^1_{X/S})^{(p)} -> 0.
- alpha comes from relative Frobenius F_{H^1}: H^{1(p)} -> H^1. Frobenius pull-back kills 1-forms, since F^*dx = d(x^p) = 0, so F_{H^1} factors through the quotient R^1f_*O^{(p)}.
- beta is defined as the transpose of alpha (written 'tF', i.e. the dual of Frobenius, V). The duality is cup product on H^1_DR together with Serre duality between R^1f_*O and f_*Omega^1.

(3) The two diagonal composites:
- F(abs) = (Hodge projection) o alpha is the Hasse-Witt map R^1f_*O^{(p)} -> R^1f_*O.
- C = beta o (Hodge inclusion) is the Cartier-Manin operator f_*Omega^1 -> f_*Omega^1^{(p)}.
- Note *****: F and C are transposes of one another up to sign, with a reference that appears to be to Cartier (and possibly Serre).

(4) The diagram is 'autodual': duality acts as point symmetry about the centre H^1_DR.

(5) Grothendieck then begins listing equivalent conditions for exactness of the row: alpha injective; beta surjective; Ker beta = Im alpha; Im alpha = (Im alpha)^perp; equality of dimensions; rank alpha = g = rank beta = rank F_{H^1}. He crosses the whole list out. What he keeps is the NB that always holds by duality: Ker alpha = (Im beta)^perp and Im alpha = (Ker beta)^perp.

The purpose is to get a global, duality-compatible description of the Cartier operator on H^1 of curves, relating F, V, Hasse-Witt and Cartier-Manin on H^1_DR. In modern terms this is the Dieudonné-module structure (F, V) on H^1_DR of a curve.
errors: The crossed-out list of equivalent conditions is vacuous. For smooth proper curves the conjugate filtration is always exact: alpha is always injective and F_{H^1} always has rank g. This follows from the Cartier isomorphism plus degeneration of the conjugate spectral sequence (Katz 1970/72; Oda 1969). This is presumably why the block was struck. The interesting non-trivial invariant (ordinarity, p-rank) lives in the diagonal maps (Hasse-Witt / Cartier-Manin), not in alpha or beta.
Note ** says H^1 is filtered 'by H^{1,0} and H^{0,1}'. Only H^{1,0} = f_*Omega^1 is a subobject; H^{0,1} = R^1f_*O is the quotient.
The precise sign in 'F and C transposed up to sign' is left unspecified.

ideas.what: Hodge and conjugate filtrations of H^1_DR of a curve in char p, drawn as a self-dual cross diagram, with alpha induced by Frobenius and beta its transpose
ideas.modern_name: Conjugate filtration / Dieudonné module structure (F, V) on H^1_DR; Hodge and conjugate filtrations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Oda (1969, 'The first de Rham cohomology group and Dieudonné modules'); Katz (1970-72, Nilpotent connections; Algebraic solutions of differential equations); Mazur; Deligne-Illusie for the general setting
ideas.where_published: Related material in Grothendieck's Montréal lectures 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1970/74) and the Katz exposé on Gauss-Manin; not this exact diagram

ideas.what: Hasse-Witt (Frobenius on R^1f_*O) and Cartier-Manin (Cartier on f_*Omega^1) are transposes under Serre duality
ideas.modern_name: Duality between Hasse-Witt matrix and Cartier-Manin matrix

ideas.what: Duality relations Ker alpha = (Im beta)^perp and Im alpha = (Ker beta)^perp under the cup-product pairing
ideas.modern_name: Self-duality of the Dieudonné module / of the conjugate filtration

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean but classical working-out of the F/V/Hodge/conjugate structure on H^1_DR of a curve. It is already in Oda (1969) and Katz (1970-72). The crossed-out passage is simply a false start, since exactness always holds.
transcription_corrections: Top of the column: 'R^1f_*(O_{X/S})' should be R^1f_*(O_X); the subscript is X/S only in a loose sense.
First line: 'lisse' is inserted above the line between 'propre' and 'de dim relative 1', i.e. 'propre lisse de dimension relative 1'.
Note ****: 'beta = tF alpha' is better read as beta = ^t(alpha), deduced from ^tF_{H^1} (the transpose of Frobenius, i.e. V) by restriction.

Note *****: the end reads roughly 'F et C sont transposés l'un de l'autre, à un signe près, [cf. Serre?] et Cartier'. The reference to Cartier (and possibly Serre) is a citation, not 'dualité de Cartier'.
The crossed-out block begins 'On a βα = 0, et on a équivalence entre les conditions'; the final line reads 'Pour ceci, il suffit que'.
